strengths: Cell-MNN offers a compact, practically motivated architecture combining state-conditioned linear operators, analytical propagation, and distribution matching without dataset-wide optimal transport preprocessing.

Interpolation results are promising: Table 1 reports the best average EMD (0.741 versus 0.776 for OT-MFM), with improvements on EB and Multi. Including the strong OT-Interpolate baseline and rerunning DeepRUOT with consistent preprocessing are valuable.

The experiments cover interpolation, joint training, synthetic scaling, and biological agreement. Hyperparameters, hardware, and additional numerical results are documented, and the ethics statement appropriately treats predicted interactions as hypotheses.
weaknesses: The central mechanistic interpretation is not established. A factorization f(z,t)=A(z,t)z is generally nonunique, and A is not generally the local Jacobian: differentiating the vector field introduces derivatives of A. Consequently, entries of V A Vᵀ are model coefficients, not automatically regulatory effects. Snapshot marginal matching further underdetermines the dynamics. Appendix D establishes existence of a factorization, not identification of biological interactions.

The stated invertibility regularizer is mathematically problematic. The loss 1/(det(P)+epsilon) is unbounded below as det(P) approaches -epsilon from below and does not guarantee invertibility or good conditioning. This undermines the claimed numerical safeguard for the eigendecomposition and requires correction or clarification.

The analytical solution is exact only for a frozen operator, not for the proposed state- and time-dependent nonlinear dynamics. Predictions made directly over an interval need not agree with predictions obtained by updating the operator at intermediate states. No step-size, composition-consistency, or approximation-error experiment supports using this local model over the full prediction horizons. The assumption f(0,t)=0 is also unmotivated for PCA coordinates.

The TRRUST evaluation is too limited to substantiate gene-interaction discovery. It classifies signs only on known edges for six model-selected source genes; it does not evaluate edge recovery. There are no established GRN baselines, correlation controls, or class-frequency-aware baselines. A universal 50% guessing reference is insufficient for F1 without specifying class balance and averaging. The zero-eigenvalue variant also worsens JUN and slightly worsens FOS, so its claimed significant improvement needs a more careful aggregate analysis.

Essential ablations are missing. A matched neural ODE trained with the same MMD and kinetic losses, a global linear model, and PCA-dimension sensitivity would help distinguish architectural gains from objective and preprocessing choices. The reported variability across held-out time points does not establish the statistical reliability of improvements across seeds. It is also unclear whether early stopping and hyperparameter selection use an independent validation split.

The scaling evidence uses resampled, noise-perturbed versions of existing datasets rather than genuinely larger biological datasets. There are no comparative runtime or memory scaling curves, and evaluation uses the same MMD kernel optimized by Cell-MNN. Improvements over Batch-OT-CFM are small on Cite and EB relative to reported variability, limiting the strength of the scalability and robustness claims.

The amortization experiment demonstrates joint fitting of two indexed datasets in separately constructed PCA spaces, not transfer to unseen datasets. Performance is essentially unchanged from separate Cell-MNN training, and stronger baselines are excluded largely for implementation convenience. This provides limited evidence for the proposed foundation-model direction.

strengths: The method offers a useful computational design: state-conditioned linear operators allow analytic local evolution and training directly against snapshot distributions without dataset-wide optimal transport preprocessing.

Interpolation results are competitive. Table 1 reports the best average EMD (0.741 versus 0.776 for OT-MFM), wins on EB and Multi, and improvements over the informative OT-Interpolate baseline on all three datasets.

The evaluation includes joint training, a minibatch OT baseline for enlarged datasets, and exploratory biological validation. Architecture and optimization settings are described in reasonable detail.
weaknesses: The central mechanistic interpretation is not established. A factorization f(z,t)=A(z,t)z is generally nonunique and does not imply that A is the local Jacobian: derivatives of A contribute to the Jacobian of f. Appendix D proves existence of a factorization, not recovery of regulatory interactions. Matching snapshot marginals further leaves individual trajectories underdetermined.

The gene-space derivation in Section 2.1 incorrectly presents projection as an equivalence: V^T dx/dt=A V^T x does not imply dx/dt=V A V^T x without restricting dynamics to the PCA subspace. The resulting rank-at-most-five operator describes reconstructed expression dynamics; its entries are not thereby validated as direct gene regulatory effects.

The invertibility regularizer is mathematically problematic as written. The objective 1/(det(P)+epsilon) is unbounded below near det(P)=-epsilon, remains finite at singular P, and does not control conditioning. It therefore does not ensure the invertibility or numerical stability claimed for the eigendecomposition.

The biological evaluation is too limited to substantiate interaction discovery. It classifies signs only for already-known edges from six selected source genes, without testing edge recovery or comparing against established GRN methods and simple correlation baselines. Class proportions, the F1 averaging convention, and a justified chance or majority baseline are missing. A universal 50% guessing reference is not generally valid for F1.

The claimed local ODE interpretation needs validation. Holding A fixed gives an exact solution only for the frozen linear system, not the state-dependent dynamics. There are no step-size, operator-refresh, or trajectory-consistency experiments establishing accuracy across the evaluated time gaps. The assumption f(0,t)=0 is also not justified for the PCA coordinates.

The scalability evidence is narrow: datasets are enlarged through resampling and noise, with no runtime or peak-memory scaling curves. Full-dataset OT runs fail, but the relevant Batch-OT-CFM baseline performs similarly on Cite and EB. Evaluation uses the same MMD kernel as Cell-MNN's training objective, without an independent metric or noise-level sweep.

Important experimental controls are missing. There is no matched neural-ODE or direct-map baseline trained with the same MMD and kinetic losses, and little ablation beyond fixing one eigenvalue. Table 1 reports variation across held-out time points rather than uncertainty in paired improvements across seeds. The separation between hyperparameter selection, early stopping, and final held-out evaluation is insufficiently specified.

The amortization experiment demonstrates joint fitting of two observed datasets using separate PCA spaces and a dataset identifier, without held-out-dataset transfer or a clear improvement over separate training. It provides limited support for broader transfer-learning claims. Overall, the predictive results are promising, but unresolved mathematical issues and insufficient mechanistic validation place the paper below the acceptance threshold.

strengths: Cell-MNN offers a useful architectural combination: state-conditioned linear operators, analytic evolution in a compact latent space, and end-to-end distribution matching without dataset-wide optimal transport preprocessing.

Interpolation results are promising. Table 1 reports the best average EMD (0.741 versus 0.776 for OT-MFM), the best results on EB and Multi, and improvements over the informative OT-Interpolate baseline on all three datasets.

The experiments cover interpolation, joint training, scaling, and biological interpretation. Rerunning DeepRUOT with consistent preprocessing and including minibatch OT in the scaling comparison are good evaluation choices.
The manuscript provides substantial training details and an exploratory validation against an external regulatory database, including an ablation of the zero-eigenvalue constraint.
weaknesses: The central gene-interaction interpretation is not established. A state-dependent factorization f(z,t)=A(z,t)z is generally nonunique, and A is not generally the Jacobian of f: derivatives of A also contribute. Consequently, entries of VAV^T need not represent regulatory effects. Moreover, the equivalence asserted in Section 2.1 between projected dynamics and full gene-space dynamics is invalid without restricting the latter to the PCA subspace; discarded directions remain unconstrained. The resulting rank-at-most-five operator requires much stronger justification as a model of gene regulation.

The invertibility regularizer is mathematically problematic as written. Minimizing 1/(det(P)+epsilon) permits negative values and an objective unbounded below near det(P)=-epsilon. It neither guarantees invertibility nor controls conditioning. Because eigenvector rescaling can change this penalty without changing A, its connection to numerical stability is additionally unclear. This needs a corrected formulation and stability evidence.

The theoretical result proves a state-dependent factorization under f(0,t)=0, not that freezing its coefficient matrix produces an accurate local linearization over the experimental time intervals. The origin-equilibrium assumption is unjustified for PCA coordinates. Independently predicted frozen-operator trajectories also need not form a consistent flow when restarted at intermediate states. No operator-refresh, interval-length, or trajectory-consistency experiment resolves this gap.

TRRUST validation tests activation/repression signs only on already-known edges for six selected source genes; it does not evaluate discovery of network structure. Class frequencies and the F1 averaging convention are unspecified, so the plotted 50% guessing reference is insufficiently justified. Majority-class, correlation/PCA, dedicated GRN, and neural-ODE Jacobian baselines are missing. The reported agreement therefore provides limited evidence that the learned operators recover mechanisms rather than expression associations.

Important attribution and evaluation controls are missing. There is no matched neural-ODE or direct prediction baseline trained with the same MMD objective, nor substantial ablations of latent dimension, kinetic regularization, or operator parameterization. Reported deviations are across held-out time points rather than seed-level uncertainty in paired improvements. The manuscript also does not clearly distinguish the data used for hyperparameter selection and early stopping from the held-out marginals used for final evaluation.

The scaling evidence is narrow: datasets are expanded by resampling and adding noise at one target size, and evaluation switches to the same MMD kernel optimized by Cell-MNN. Improvements over Batch-OT-CFM are small relative to reported variation on Cite and EB. Runtime and peak-memory curves, real larger datasets, and an independent evaluation metric are needed to substantiate broad scalability and noise-robustness claims.

Joint training demonstrates that one model can fit two known datasets, but does not establish transfer or a distinctive amortization advantage. The datasets use separate PCA coordinates and dataset identifiers, with no unseen-dataset evaluation; Cell-MNN's joint performance is essentially unchanged from separate training. Overall, the predictive results are encouraging, but unresolved mathematical and biological-validation issues prevent the paper from meeting the acceptance threshold.
